what_its_for: Formoterol is a long-acting bronchodilator (airway opener) used to help control and prevent breathing problems caused by asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). It helps relax the muscles around your airways, making it easier to breathe. It is NOT a rescue inhaler — it will not work fast enough to treat a sudden asthma attack.
how_to_take: Formoterol comes as a dry powder inhaler capsule (Foradil) or a liquid solution for a nebulizer (Perforomist). For the inhaler: Pierce the capsule inside the device, breathe out fully away from the inhaler, place the mouthpiece in your mouth, seal your lips around it, and breathe in quickly and deeply. Hold your breath for 5–10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. Never swallow the capsules — they are only for use in the inhaler device. For the nebulizer: Pour the liquid into the nebulizer cup, attach the mask or mouthpiece, and breathe in the mist normally until the cup is empty. Always rinse your mouth with water after use to help prevent throat irritation.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one capsule (12 mcg) inhaled twice daily, about 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). For COPD with the nebulizer solution, the usual dose is 20 mcg (one vial) inhaled twice daily. Always take it at the same times each day. Do not take more than 2 doses in 24 hours. Do not use more than prescribed — using too much can be dangerous.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take 2 doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store the capsules or vials at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C–25°C). Keep capsules in their original foil blister pack and only remove them right before use. Protect from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep out of reach of children. For nebulizer vials: if opened, use immediately; do not save for later use.
what_to_avoid: Do not use formoterol as a rescue inhaler during a sudden asthma attack — always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler (like albuterol) on hand. Do not use more than prescribed. Avoid smoking, as it can make your breathing condition worse. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other bronchodilators, beta-blockers (like metoprolol), diuretics (water pills), or antidepressants, as these can interact with formoterol. Avoid excessive caffeine, as it may increase the risk of side effects like a fast heartbeat or shakiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden worsening of breathing or wheezing, chest pain or a pounding/racing heartbeat, you need your rescue inhaler more often than usual, severe headache, dizziness, or shakiness, signs of low potassium such as muscle cramps or weakness, or swelling of your face, lips, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction). Also contact your doctor if your breathing does not seem to be improving over time.
when_it_works: Formoterol does not work instantly. It may take 1 to 3 minutes to start working after inhalation, but its main benefit builds up over time with regular daily use. It is designed to prevent breathing problems over a 12-hour period, not to stop an attack once it has started. You should notice improved day-to-day breathing control within the first few days of regular use.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using formoterol if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: Formoterol is generally approved for children 5 years and older for asthma, but only use it in children under close medical supervision. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as fast heartbeat or tremors — report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Heart conditions or diabetes: Use with caution, as formoterol can raise blood sugar and affect heart rhythm. Tell your doctor about all health conditions before starting this medication.
